Each completed Stream DEM is saved automatically as an immutable local edition.
The app reuses an edition while its input binding and processing recipe still
match. Saving outputs is part of processing, not a separate analyst action.

## Storage contract

`local_study_store()` delegates DEM persistence to `study_dem_store()`. Editions
live under `<study>/event-dems/editions/<id>/` and contain
`dem-international-feet.tif` plus an internal `edition.rds` record. Available
mosaic/masked intermediates can also be retained. Raster paths resolve within the
managed edition; source paths remain provenance.

FGDB ADR-0025 requires external filesystem GeoTIFF DEMs with GeoPackage vectors,
tables and linked metadata. The RDS record serializes the app's local edition
index; it is not the portable FGDB folder manifest. Portable folder binding,
relocation qualification and enterprise transfer remain separate work. The
accepted storage references are linked from `dev/schemas/survey-event-dem.md`.

## Identity and publication

The binding identifies the Study context, Event definition and Collection
selection revisions. The recipe records target identity/scope, source and mask
file identity, source selection/order, extent, units and backend version.
Supported scopes are Stream, Reach and bounded portions of either.

Workers write into unique Study-owned staging directories. Before publication,
the controller rechecks saved binding and input recipe. A completed record and
directory rename publish the edition on the same volume. A new run never
overwrites an existing edition. An already verified cached DEM may be copied in
a worker rather than calculated again.

Cancellation, failure and session closure stop workers before deleting owned
staging. Cleanup rejects published edition paths and paths outside the managed
root. Recorded app/worker ownership supports abandoned-stage recovery only when
both processes have exited.

## Reopening and reuse

`find_dem(binding, recipe=NULL, stream_id=NULL, scope=NULL)` selects an eligible
edition. Normal Event tabs request their own Stream and full-Stream scope. The
reader checks the small record, raster presence and byte size. Saved-source
identity checks exclude changed selections. It does not scan all raster values
or repeat transfer hashes on every view.

Missing or corrupt editions are skipped. Strict revision binding excludes outputs
from earlier settings revisions; metadata-only reuse across revisions is not
implemented. Older Reach/portion records remain readable. Available intermediate
paths are resolved within their actual edition; absent intermediates are not
required to display a saved final DEM.

## Implementation and tests

Trace `R/study_dem_store.R`, its adapters in `R/study_store.R`, publication in
`R/terrain_dem_trial.R` and display in `R/terrain_mosaic_trial.R`.
`test-study-dem-store.R` covers exact-file publication, fresh reopening, stale
binding exclusion and cleanup protection. Source and queue tests cover selection
changes and independent Stream lookup. The exact record contract is
`dev/schemas/survey-event-dem.md`.

## Data objects and storage

See [Data objects and local storage](storage-model.html) for the FGDB ownership and physical representation crosswalk.

| Operation | Data object read or changed | Physical representation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publish_dem` | Publishes a complete local terrain edition with input associations | External GeoTIFF and internal edition metadata |
| `find_dem` / result reader | Resolves the eligible terrain for Stream/context inputs | Reads local edition metadata and GeoTIFF; no domain identity change |
| FGDB delivery adapter | Would bind governed Reach/Event products and shared sources to delivery metadata | GeoPackage vectors/tables plus external GeoTIFFs and portable manifest; adapter not implemented |

Local output editions are not automatically FGDB accepted dataset editions. The
internal RDS index is not a geodatabase feature class or the long-term delivery
manifest. Governed product identity, ownership and acceptance follow FGDB contracts.

Stream terrain editions are intended to be shared by consuming Reach analyses.
A Reach/Event association should identify the selected edition rather than require
a duplicate raster. FGDB relationship and delivery bindings need to express this
direction; the current internal edition index does not implement them.
